plotSections.title: Haldor's send-off
bullets: Haldor says the mines across the lake are opening again, bringing competition and all kinds of traffic through New Navel.
Sylan does not think the celestials are part of this matter. He allows there may be more to learn and sets that aside; he is satisfied Haldor has answered his questions.
The party plans to have dinner, make plans, and leave. They are on a mission and do not expect to stay long. Haldor needs nothing from them and says Gerk can explain.

Haldor tells them to keep Gerk's companion away from the ghosts, keep commotion outside town, and not to open doors here—not even to the tavern. Friends may open a door so the party can walk in. He refuses Gerk's windows joke, says he does not have the paperwork for that, and heads back to his porch.

plotSections.title: Street talk before the cut
bullets: Gerk shows Sylan the wicker chicken and says he paid one gold. Sylan thinks it is well made.

Sylan wants to take the long way to Shades and Trades to be sure he did not miss anyone. Gerk says Haldor told him to stay out of town and garbles the warning about his companion and the ghosts. Sylan thinks that situation is already cleared up.
Gerk thinks Carlkin wants them arrested. Sylan jokes that Gerk might enjoy court, then starts to walk off. The DM pauses that thread and returns to the lighthouse.

plotSections.title: The helm is soulbound, not a phylactery
bullets: Carlkin has been measuring the helm and taking notes. He grinds reagents in a mortar and pestle, mixes them with a brackish pond-water liquid, and shakes it until it turns crystal clear in a two-to-three-ounce vial.

He calls the result a soul identifier, akin to the bag test but meant to give a finer reading. A phylactery would have gone off violently, burst into flames, and provoked a magical reaction. This helm did not.
A drop of the liquid beads on the helm and stays put instead of running off. Through a magnifying glass, Carlkin finds spiritual residue on it.

Walker says that after he killed the wearer, he spoke with him: a hobgoblin in purple robes, calm and respectful, not spooky. The figure treated Walker's golden fire as his life force and as something that mattered to him as well, and he wants people to rule as they did before the Voyager gods.

Carlkin, a tortle, has Walker cough and checks his pulse. The helm carries a fragment or soul memory. Walker has interacted with the soul bound to it and is slightly affected, but he is not heavily possessed and it is not parasitic yet.

Walker puts the helm back on and treats it as his. Dana objects. Carlkin floats having Gerk try it, then says Gerk should never wear it. Keep it from high-ranking clerics of light domains and from feeble-minded wearers, who would be affected more.

Warning signs that the possession is worsening: queasiness, numb earlobes, a tingling left armpit, or voices other than Walker's own, his inner voice, or Glimmen. Walker adds Araden and Elrus as voices he already hears.

Carlkin says the lich died wearing the helm, leaving a tiny imprint of his being or remembrance. That imprint is why the helm burned Carlkin's bag, though not quickly. Walker asks whether they can use the fragment to track him. He looks for a soul-worker he thought had come along; Sylan says that person did not. The scene cuts off as the DM starts to place Sylan.

chronologicalEvents: 1. Haldor tells Sylan the mines across the lake are reopening and traffic through New Navel is up.
2. Sylan sets the celestials aside for later and says his questions are answered. Haldor asks how long the party will stay.
3. Sylan says they will eat, plan, and leave soon because they are on a mission. Haldor needs nothing and defers to Gerk.
4. Haldor warns them to keep Gerk's companion off the ghosts, bans doors in town, tells them to keep commotion outside town, and returns to his porch. Gerk jokes that he will use only windows.
5. Gerk shows Sylan the wicker chicken he bought for one gold. Sylan starts for Shades and Trades the long way so he does not miss anyone.
6. Gerk says Haldor told him to stay out of town and that Carlkin wants them arrested. Sylan jokes about court and walks off.
7. The DM cuts back to Carlkin's lighthouse, where Carlkin has been measuring the helm and mixing a soul identifier.
8. Carlkin drips the clear reagent on the helm. It beads and sticks. He finds spiritual residue and asks Walker about a spiritual encounter when he picked it up.
9. Walker recounts a calm talk, after the killing, with a hobgoblin in purple robes who spoke of golden fire and of ruling as people did before the Voyager gods.
10. Carlkin checks Walker's cough and pulse and tells Dana the helm holds a soul memory: slight contact, not a heavy or parasitic possession.
11. Walker puts the helm back on. Carlkin forbids Gerk from ever wearing it, warns against light clerics and feeble-minded wearers, and lists signs that possession is getting worse.

12. Carlkin explains the lich died in the helm and left a tiny imprint, which slowly burned his bag. Walker proposes using that fragment to track the lich. Sylan says the soul-worker Walker means did not come with them.

Haldor.existing: Sheriff of New Navel who bans doors and spirit-taking inside the city.
notes: Says mines on the other side of the lake are opening again, with enough competition and traffic that all sorts pass through New Navel.
Asks how long the party will stay. He does not need anything from them and leaves the explanation to Gerk.

Repeats the door ban, including doorways to the tavern: friends may open a door so the party can walk in, but the party is not to open doors. He also tells them to keep Gerk's companion away from the ghosts and to keep commotion outside town.
Turns down Gerk's windows joke because he does not have the paperwork for that kind of effect. He goes back to his porch.
Sylan calls him Boss. Gerk takes the warning as an order to stay out of town.
personality: Polite but firm about the town rules, and finished with the party once those rules are restated.
quotesThemes: No doors. Have your friends open it and just walk in.
Keep the commotion outside of town.

notes: Does not think the celestials are part of the current matter, but suspects there is more to learn and does not pursue it now.
Plans for the party to have dinner, make plans, and leave soon. They are on a mission.
After Haldor leaves, he wants to walk the long way to Shades and Trades to make sure he did not miss anyone. He thinks the sheriff's objection to them being in town is already settled.
He is present for the helm reading, agrees Gerk should not wear it, and says the soul-worker Walker hoped to use did not come with them.
Haldor tells him not to open doors in town and to keep his companion away from the ghosts. Gerk answers with a windows-only joke, which Haldor refuses.
Shows Sylan the wicker chicken and says it cost one gold.
He believes Haldor ordered him to stay out of town, and he thinks Carlkin wants the party arrested.
Carlkin says Gerk should never wear the helm. A feeble-minded wearer would take the possession harder, and Carlkin does not want the emperor's fragment in Gerk.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen.
notes: After killing the helm's wearer, he spoke with him. The talk was calm and respectful. Walker remembers a hobgoblin in purple robes.

The figure called Walker's golden fire his life force and treated that power as something that mattered to him as well. He wants people to rule as they did before the Voyager gods. Walker remembers nothing else that stood out.
Carlkin finds only slight possession: Walker has touched the soul bound to the helm, and it has not turned parasitic.
Walker puts the helm back on anyway and says it stays on his head. He asks if the fragment can be used to track the lich, and he looks for a soul-worker he thought had traveled with the party.
Voices he already treats as normal include his own, Glimmen, Araden, and Elrus. Those are the exceptions Carlkin is given for the possession warning.
quotesThemes: The golden fire is his life force as a gold dragon rider.
The fragment might be used to track the lich.
openQuestions: Can the soul fragment in the helm be used to find the lich?

notes: Carlkin addresses the helm result to her: a soul memory is attached, which is concerning, but Walker is not heavily possessed.
She calls that a small relief and tells Walker not to put the helm back on.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like scholar; the party brought him the helm to examine.
notes: At the lighthouse he measures the helm, takes notes, and mixes a soul identifier in a mortar and pestle. The mix starts as a brackish, pond-like liquid and is shaken clear in a two-to-three-ounce vial.
The reagent is meant to work like the earlier bag test while giving a finer reading of what the object is.
The drop beads on the helm instead of running off. He sees spiritual residue and calls the attachment a fragment or soul memory.
He has Walker cough and takes his pulse. His conclusion is slight possession from contact with the bound soul, not a heavy or parasitic possession.
He says the item is soulbound because the lich died wearing it, leaving a tiny imprint of his being or remembrance. That imprint is why the helm burned Carlkin's bag, though slowly.
He warns Walker to watch for queasiness, numb earlobes, tingling in the left armpit, and voices other than his own, his inner voice, or Glimmen.
He says to keep the helm from clerics of high standing in light domains, and from feeble-minded wearers. He specifically says Gerk should never put it on.
Gerk believes Carlkin wants the party arrested. Carlkin does not say that in this scene.
personality: Clinical about the helm, briefly tempted to test it on Gerk, then firm that Gerk must not wear it.
quotesThemes: This is a soul identifier, not evidence of a phylactery.
There is slight possession, and it does not appear parasitic yet.
Gerk should not put that helmet on ever.

notes: Walker’s name for the hobgoblin in purple robes he killed and then spoke with after picking up the helm. Carlkin treats that wearer as the lich who died in the helmet.
The conversation Walker remembers was calm and respectful. The figure spoke of Walker's golden fire as his life force and as something that mattered to the figure as well.
He wants people to rule as they did before the Voyager gods.
A very small fragment, memory, or imprint of him remains soulbound to the helm. It is not a phylactery. Contact has left Walker slightly affected, not yet in a parasitic possession.
Carlkin does not want that fragment tested on Gerk.
personality: Calm and respectful in the talk Walker remembers. He wants rule restored to the way it was before the Voyager gods, and Walker's golden fire matters to him.
quotesThemes: People should rule as they did before the Voyager gods.
Walker's golden fire is his life force.

Helm.existing: A helm Carlkin agreed to examine.
notes: Not a phylactery. Carlkin says a phylactery would have exploded, burst into flames, and caused a magical reaction.
A soul identifier drop beads on the crown and stays there. Carlkin reads spiritual residue: a fragment or soul memory of the lich who died wearing it.
The imprint is why it burned Carlkin's bag, and why it burned slowly.
Walker has interacted with the bound soul. Carlkin calls the effect slight possession and not yet parasitic.
Walker puts it back on and says it should stay on his head. Carlkin forbids Gerk from wearing it, and warns against high light-domain clerics and feeble-minded wearers.
Escalation signs Carlkin gives Walker: queasiness, numbing of the earlobes, tingling of the left armpit, and voices other than Walker's, his inner voice, or Glimmen.
Walker suggests the fragment could be used to track the lich. That is not answered in this chunk.
openQuestions: Can the bound fragment be used to track the lich?

Soul identifier.existing: Carlkin's reagent for a finer reading of an object's spiritual residue.
notes: Carlkin mixes it during the exam. He grinds materials with a mortar and pestle, adds a brackish liquid that looks like pond water, and shakes it until it is crystal clear.
The dose is a small vial, about two to three ounces. He describes it as similar to the bag test, with a finer reading.
Dripped on the helm, it pools at the point of contact and does not run down the metal. That reaction leads him to the spiritual residue and soul-memory reading.

Golden fire.existing: The life force of Walker's gold dragon rider bond.
notes: Walker tells Carlkin that the hobgoblin emperor referred to the golden fire as Walker's life force, the magical energy of his gold dragon rider bond.
Walker says that energy matters to the emperor as it matters to Walker. He does not remember the emperor saying more than that about it.

Voyager Gods.existing: Gods from other pantheons who did not originate in Atlas.
notes: Walker says the emperor wants people to rule as they did before the Voyager gods.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop with Carlkin's lighthouse and trade caravans bound for the party's tavern in Langdale.
notes: Haldor says mines on the other side of the lake are opening again, bringing competition and heavy, mixed traffic.
He again bars doors inside town, tells the party to keep a companion away from the ghosts, and tells them to keep commotion outside town. He leaves toward his porch.

Shades and Trades.existing: Where Sylan found the staff later fused to Ord's lantern.
notes: Sylan plans to walk there the long way through town to make sure he did not miss anyone. The DM pauses that errand before he arrives.

Celestial echo.existing: New Navel's dead who return as celestial forms of themselves, not ghosts or undead.
notes: Sylan does not think the celestials were part of the matter he was asking Haldor about. He says there may still be something to learn and that he has no time for it now.
